data.raw_text:
Shame on us. (Bill Hornbuckle, CEO, MGM Resorts)

Credit where credit is due. Bill said the quiet part out loud. That stated, are casinos really to blame for the downward spiral Las Vegas ?

Casinos are "For Profit" Companies - Economics 101 states that pricing is determined by supply and demand. Due to $7T in free government money, there was overwhelming demand for gambling, expensive dinners, and Louis Vuitton handbags. Casinos raised their prices...because they could.

Americans Continued the Party - When the government subsidies ran out, Americans raided their savings and drew down their 401Ks. Casinos raised prices again.

Who is the Real Problem? - Submitted for your consideration: Are the casinos the problem, or is it the Americans that are willing to pay the outrageous prices for hotel rooms dining, and show tickets? Casinos will keep raising prices until customers stop coming to Las Vegas and refuse to pay them.

Our Locals Strategy - As Locals, we almost never go to the Las Vegas Strip. Traffic, paid parking, overpriced restaurants and outrageous show ticket prices. Oh...hell no! Personally, I'm a big Red Rock Resort fan, but pick any Station Casinos or Boyd Gaming property. Even the Palms. Free parking, reasonable prices and much better comps.

Casino Alternatives - We recently took a Princess Cruise. Great casino! There is Resorts World at Sea in Asia. Personally, I love Manila and Macau. If you are in San Diego - the Sycuan or Pechanga. In Florida - Hard Rock Hollywood. Why would you fly to Las Vegas to experience price gouging?

Now, let's go make some money!

data.raw_text:
Cemeteries in the Philippines are literally disappearing underwater. In Hagonoy, Bulacan, rising seas and constant flooding have left graves permanently submerged. 

Families can’t even visit their loved ones anymore because the water never recedes. 

It’s a clear and powerful sign of how climate change is reshaping life and death in vulnerable places like this.
